mechanism: Public randomized diagonal phases and one inverse-F3 realize the full-root covariant POVM without quantum ancillas. Fixed inverse-F3 records reuse exact joint likelihood algebra but have a distinct full-label centered Gram, including a zero-secret exception.
research_decision: At M=nr-2, reject fixed product inverse-F3 followed by arbitrary classical decoding as a constant population-advantage route. Do not extend this exclusion to other measurement policies or polynomial surplus samples.
falsifiers: An arbitrary-input randomized branch effect differs from the covariant effect divided by three.
Full-label and output character orthogonality contradicts the exact nonzero-secret, zero-secret or off-diagonal Gram.
The exact phase-algebra adapter gives a different posterior from the actual fixed-trine likelihood.
The physical all-secret native twirl disagrees with the exact joint correlation countercontrol.

proof_obligations.PO-REVIEW: Independently review the randomized effect identity, Gram over the composite ring, omitted-zero contribution and classifier copy bound.
proof_obligations.PO-MODEL: Keep fixed-trine data distinct from paired covariant data; an observation-wise likelihood constant transfers the posterior, not the generative law or copy bound.
proof_obligations.PO-SOURCE: The population theorem requires IID full even-level native rows and independent original copies. Unique ancestor IDs alone do not prove this.
proof_obligations.PO-SCOPE: Do not claim a bound on all product bases, adaptive LOCC, collective receivers, chosen labels, sieve-retained laws or polynomial surplus copies.
proof_obligations.PO-COMPLEXITY: Exact joint decoding remains exponential. The randomized compiler saves measurement ancillas but does not solve decoding or supply source states.
proof_obligations.PO-PRECISION: Charge public phase synthesis, F3 implementation and classical randomness errors; hardware gate export is not supplied.
proof_obligations.PO-NOVELTY: No novelty or speedup claim. Prespecified small native labels are proof countercontrols, not algorithm candidates.
